questions.text: Which planet is closest to the Sun, and how long is its year?
questions.answer: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, and its sidereal year is 88 Earth days.

questions.text: At what does Aristotle's philosophy aim?
questions.answer: Aristotle's philosophy aims at the universal.

questions.text: With which work is Aristotle credited with the earliest systematic study of logic?
questions.answer: With the Prior Analytics, Aristotle is credited with the earliest systematic study of logic.

questions.text: Across which areas does the bald eagle range?
questions.answer: The bald eagle ranges across most of North America, including most of Canada, all of the contiguous United States, and northern Mexico.

questions.text: As the national symbol of the United States, the bald eagle is prominent in which items?
questions.answer: The bald eagle is prominent in seals and logos, coinage, postage stamps, and other items relating to the U.S. federal government.

questions.text: What did Ibn Battuta call the island when he visited in the 14th century?
questions.answer: Ibn Battuta referred to the island as Kalanpu.

questions.text: Which language is Delhi's most spoken, at 80.94%?
questions.answer: Hindi

questions.text: In game theory, which game involves two players of different sexes with different preferences?
questions.answer: The "battle of the sexes" game involves two players of different sexes, arbitrarily chosen, each with a different set of preferences.

questions.text: What is a Nash equilibrium, in terms of how every player responds to the others?
questions.answer: A Nash equilibrium is a stable state in which each player is playing a best response to the strategies of the other players, such that no player has an incentive to unilaterally deviate from their choice.

questions.text: Through what does the muscular organ found in humans and other animals pump blood?
questions.answer: The muscular organ found in humans and other animals that pumps blood is the heart.

questions.text: Into which four chambers is the human heart divided?
questions.answer: The human heart is divided into four chambers: upper left and right atria and lower left and right ventricles.

questions.text: Which two genomes are usually treated separately?
questions.answer: The human genome is usually treated separately into the nuclear genome and the mitochondrial genome.

questions.text: On average, how many DNA damage events does the human genome experience per cell per day?
questions.answer:
Based on the evidence provided, the human genome experiences tens of thousands of DNA damage events per day on average. This can be seen in the following sentence from the evidence:

"In each cell of the human body, the human genome experiences, on average, tens of thousands of DNA damage events per day. These damage events can block genome replication or genome transcription, and if they are not repaired or are repaired incorrectly, they may lead to mutations, or other genome alterations in the human genome that threaten cell viability."

questions.text: The colour that derives its name from a fruit shares its name with a crop whose 2024 world production of 67 million tonnes was led by which country?
questions.answer: The colour orange that derives its name from a fruit shares its name with a crop whose 2024 world production of 67 million tonnes was led by Brazil.

questions.text: The general who rose to prominence during the French Revolution became First Consul by engineering which coup?
questions.answer: The general who rose to prominence during the French Revolution and became First Consul by engineering the Coup of 18 Brumaire was Napoleon Bonaparte. This coup occurred on 9 November 1799, which was the 18th of Brumaire according to the French Revolutionary calendar.

questions.text: The town along the eastern approach to Sherman Hill Summit, the highest point of the transcontinental Interstate 80, provides access to reach which monument?
questions.answer: The town along the eastern approach to Sherman Hill Summit, the highest point of the transcontinental Interstate 80, provides access to reach the Ames Monument, which marks the highest point along the original routing of the First transcontinental railroad.

questions.text: The city with the 65 ha Beira Lake in its heart has an airport located how far south of the city centre?
questions.answer: The city with the 65 ha Beira Lake in its heart has an airport located 15 km south of the city centre.

questions.text: The basin located in west equatorial Africa has a rainforest second in size only to which forest?
questions.answer: The Congo Basin has a rainforest second in size only to the Amazon rainforest.

questions.text: The crater that has been burning since 1971 was first descended to the bottom by a person gathering soil samples for which project?
questions.answer: The crater that has been burning since 1971 was first descended to the bottom by a person gathering soil samples for the Extreme Microbiome Project.

questions.text: Which cybersecurity company did Orange acquire in 2019?
questions.answer: Orange acquired SecureLink, a Netherlands-based cybersecurity company, in 2019 for €515 million.

questions.text: What is the capital of South Africa?
questions.answer: The capital of South Africa is Pretoria.

questions.text: Between Napoleon's self-coronation as Emperor of the French and the February Revolution that inaugurated the Russian Revolution, which event came first?
questions.answer: The February Revolution that inaugurated the Russian Revolution came first. This event occurred in 1917, while Napoleon's self-coronation as Emperor of the French took place in 1804.

questions.text: Between the West Indian manatee and the Amazonian manatee, which is the only exclusively freshwater manatee?
questions.answer: The Amazonian manatee (Trichechus inunguis) is the only exclusively freshwater manatee.

questions.text: On what exact date in 1866 was the original town of Buford founded?
questions.answer: The original town of Buford was founded in 1866.

questions.text: On what exact date did engineers ignite the Darvaza gas crater?
questions.answer: According to the evidence provided, engineers ignited the Darvaza gas crater in the 1980s. Specifically, the relevant text states: "Others assert that the site was drilled by Soviet engineers in 1971 as an oil field but collapsed within days, forming the crater, with the engineers choosing to flare the crater to prevent the emission of poisonous gases but underestimating the volume of the gas."
